reapack.name: BandSync.lua
reapack.desc: BandSync: record together remotely over a shared folder

version.author: James
version.changelog: First release: publish/open/send/inbox, rooms, lanes, versioned stems, local copies, 24-bit FLAC recording, latency calibration, version checks and updater, AI installer.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Send works per take: sends the active take you picked (send again after picking another); new 'Send all takes' sends every unsent pass, grouped. Sent status tracked per take, so re-recording into a sent item is caught. Selection check compares takes, not counts. Unique take IDs within the same second (fixes a REAPER 'files exist' freeze). Per-song comping style (lanes/takes) detected at publish; takes mode adds incoming takes to the matching item without moving existing audio.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live sync (replaces Take inbox): every recording goes out by itself when you stop, all passes, printed at the item's exact extent; everyone's takes are rebuilt in the same tracks, lanes and multi-take items; the host shares its existing takes and lanes. Print modes wet (default) / dry / both, with FX-free mirror tracks for wet prints. Takes reprint as new revisions when FX, volume, pan or fades change. The session driver's deletes, moves, trims, lane moves and lane/take choices propagate; 'Take control' passes driving. New Status window with two-way receipts. Fixes: 'dry' prints went through the track (now truly dry), lane play state restore, dry twins on preview upgrade, take deletes in background tabs.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Update (shared-folder installs) also removes actions whose scripts no longer exist, e.g. the old Take inbox.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Status: ages were an hour off in daylight-saving time zones, so everyone showed offline and your own Live sync 'not running'.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Copy/paste, duplicate and split: the copies carried the original's hidden BandSync id, so they never went out (and confused edits/deletes). Copies are now detected and sent as new takes; a split sends the left half as a trim and the right half as a new take.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live sync never shows a dialog: a newer-BandSync warning used to pause every background script (and Live sync) until clicked. It's now a console line, and the Status window shows a banner.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Deleting something and pasting it back in the same place now syncs again (the 'already sent' guard ignored that the earlier copy was deleted).

version.author: James
version.changelog: The driver's mirrored changes get their own undo point and are logged by name (deleted / moved / now playing). The Status window opens next to the mouse instead of over REAPER's menu bar.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Ownership: claim tracks or song regions so only your edits there propagate; what you can't change is view-only (locked). Recall points at every handover (and by hand): the driver can restore any of them, deleted takes come back. Hold sync. Track mute/solo/name/colour/icon and item mute follow. MIDI takes carry their notes as an editable MIDI copy; note edits sync, and 'Print my MIDI' replaces a print with your own instrument. New BandSync - Panel (needs ReaImGui): everything in one dockable window.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Panel: Stop ends Live sync directly instead of raising REAPER's task-control dialog, and running/stopped shows within seconds. Claimed track and region names keep their case.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Solo edit: check a song out to edit alone through Google Drive (lock with presence, versions with per-track changes, restore any version); wet prints kept beside dry recordings so missing plugins never lose a sound. Live tab: hear each other through REAPER's ReaNINJAM (synced play-along with placeholders on the timeline, live listen, or jam) via a NINJAM server over Tailscale. History & restore tab: every change grouped by person, restore to any point. Take control waits until everyone is in sync. Drum maps translate MIDI drums between VSTs. New sessions print wet + dry.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live placeholders: each received clip is placed once (no more place/replace loop), and only that person's takes recorded after the live session began replace them. Placeholders appear when the listener disconnects (ReaNINJAM writes its clip log then). Panel: the version banner's Update button no longer raises an ImGui ID error.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live sync starts Syncthing if it isn't running; the host's Live tab Connect starts the NINJAM server (set its folder once). Placing live placeholders makes one undo point.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Setup guide covers Live (Tailscale share), Solo edit (Google Drive shortcut) and ReaImGui; Solo edit finds Google Drive on macOS by itself

version.author: James
version.changelog: Listen live through SonoBus (peer to peer, low delay, no server, works on Mac); panel Set up list with 'Set up everything I can'; publish/open buttons on non-BandSync projects; one-click installers for Windows (tested) and macOS (untested); Save for the band no longer drops the SonoBus group

version.author: James
version.changelog: Listen live joins with one click and no paste: BandSync writes the band's SonoBus group, password and your name into SonoBus's state. One SonoBus group per band (sonobus.json in the shared folder) instead of per song.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Fixes from the PC-laptop live test: placeholders are replaced only by takes recorded while they were heard, and a newer session's clips replace an older session's; the Play along server field picks up an address the host sets later; Set up shows when REAPER's audio device is closed; the installer reopens itself outside a sandboxed app's shell.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Set up list: Syncthing connected-to-bandmates check and audio-device check; SonoBus set to a steadier jitter buffer (Auto-Increase from 40 ms) and a wired-internet hint; takes go out sooner after you stop; MIDI from a track without an instrument is flagged so receivers know why its print is silent; panel opens inside REAPER's window; installer: works under Windows PowerShell 5.1, downloads the newest release, and its closing list shows only what's left.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Tempo map and markers sync from whoever is driving, and REAPER moves everyone's items by its own timebase; take positions travel in beats; History and recall restores bring back their tempo map. Play along in a second song tab works (ReaNINJAM is moved, not duplicated). MIDI takes print through their instrument and skip the silent dry. Live clip arrival times aren't stored in the project.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Prints contain only the item: a synth routed into the track to record it no longer ends up in the print (it played twice on everyone else's machine).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Restoring a deleted take brings the owner's real item back (not a mirror of their own take); a MIDI copy never reprints without an instrument; old revisions go to _trash instead of being deleted; History shows what really changed on a track, and colour/icon changes (e.g. SWS auto-colour) no longer go out on their own.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Tempo changes no longer make song-long audio drift: band audio follows the beat by position only (moved, never stretched), MIDI parts are reprinted at the new tempo by their owners, and the driver is told which audio takes need re-recording past the change. Fixed: a handover event blocked every later change on receivers.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Tempo changes stretch band audio the way REAPER is set to, piece by piece: in REAPER's default timebase band audio uses REAPER's auto-stretch at tempo changes (unchanged before the change, stretched after it), instead of 0.7.7's position-only. Other timebases are left as the project says.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A new revision of a take plays straight (it was rendered at the current tempo): no stretch left over from the previous print.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Solo edit stops the song tab's Live sync before turning it into the working copy, and Live sync stops by itself in a working copy (it had re-sent the copied media as new takes). Solo edit versions list volume, pan, mute and routing changes, so a mix pass reads as one.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Solo versions leave out the live plug-ins (ReaNINJAM, SonoBus), which only raised load warnings; History shows tempo changes without a bogus -1/-1 time signature.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Together tab: play/record/stop together, notes and likes, live ideas, take back, print MIDI as audio, Solo edit mix, insert/remove bars, dry mode with the sender's plug-ins. Shared mix (volume/pan), reverb tails in wet prints, locked edits snap back, autostart with REAPER, trash cleanup, newest songs first.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Your own takes are yours to move/trim/mute where nobody has claimed. Mix changes made before you joined arrive. Print MIDI as audio keeps the release tail. Panel: Set up only opens for essentials, drum map folds away, bars instead of seconds, Enter posts a note, confirmations for Remove bars and Solo edit mix. History shows volume in dB.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Play/Record together hit the moment on every machine (start/stop cues are checked every 0.25 s; 5 s lead). Insert/Remove bars splits takes that cross the edit point (after asking) and keeps late-arriving takes in place. Notes show on every take of an item. Dry mode names the plug-ins this machine lacks.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Insert/Remove bars: each person splits their own takes, so both parts stay theirs and land on their tracks; MIDI copies are never split (a copy split in two re-sent its notes every 2 s). History restores bring back the tempo/markers an insert left and move MIDI copies with their prints.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Insert/Remove bars splits without losing anything (REAPER's split cuts MIDI notes away; a restore found them gone). History: a 3-minute pause starts a new group, and each group shows its first change. The update banner says when only the open panel is old.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Insert/Remove bars: the trimmed first part of each split take goes out as an edit. A take sent while muted arrives muted. MIDI copies end with their notes, not with the print's reverb tail.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Take back my last take skips the parts an insert/remove split made, and asks with the track and bars.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Panel: the last start/stop together and how close it hit; which take a note goes on; bar numbers everywhere; dry mode says whose part; Remove bars says what it cuts; plainer Live mode texts; Solo edit's folder setting moved below the versions; notes name the track.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side: everyone's normal transport drives everyone (play, stop, record, seeks), followers a set number of bars behind so Play along lets them hear the take in context; the one recording records, the rest listen. Together tab: start from a region, countdown, count-in click, who's ready (Live sync, armed tracks, side by side). Dry mode shows which of the plug-ins you have.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Fix: Live sync's status receipt called the side-by-side helper before it existed (every tick errored on 0.9.0). tests/check_locals.py now catches that.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side: a stop carries the song position, so followers stop exactly where the leader did even when the event arrives late. Panel wording fixes.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side / Together: Live sync holds its regular poll while a start or stop is due, so followers start on the moment (it could run 100-200 ms into it).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side: a follower stops only after two readings at the leader's stop position (a momentary position glitch stopped one early), and says whether it stopped by position or by time.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Fix 0.9.4: the stop debounce read the project before it was known. check_locals also guards proj/cfg/b/key.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side: an older cue can never replace a newer one (a stale stop swallowed the next start); while playing, Live sync's full pass runs every 2 s (it could stall REAPER ~0.5 s). check_locals guards every script-level variable.

version.author: James
version.changelog: No more UI stutter from status checks: whether Syncthing and the NINJAM server run, and Syncthing's connections, are now checked in the background (they froze REAPER 0.3-0.4 s at every panel refresh).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Background checks run through a hidden-window runner (0.9.7 flashed a console window). The panel warns when ReaNINJAM is sending in Normal or Voice mode, which makes Play along miss the song. A follower that plays along while the leader records says so.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Play along placeholders also work when ReaNINJAM sits on a track instead of the master. Clearer follower message while someone records. Side by side + Play along verified to line up at 0 ms between two machines.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Claim a time selection (shown as a [claimed: you] region; track > time > region > driver). NINJAM's metronome is off for Play along/Listen live, with a toggle. Solo edit: the first checkout opens a copy in its own tab (it used to turn the live session's tab into the copy); restoring a version really reloads it (it silently didn't); a solo tab shows only Solo edit; History groups Solo versions apart; no empty versions.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Break-round fixes: Solo projects save media paths relative (other machines found everything offline) and say when items couldn't be printed; a tempo change no longer reprints every take (rounding), and reprints go two at a time; a moved/trimmed revision also goes out as an edit so History has it; a copy of a bandmate's take is never sent as yours; renaming a track you don't own snaps back and edits keep the band's track name; a print missing from the shared folder is printed again; slivers are skipped out loud; Open session won't open a song twice; snap-back names the owner; plug-in chain names can't collide.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Solo edit prints are keyed by the project as saved (not live plug-in values), so another machine's check-in doesn't reprint unchanged parts. Paste messages fixed; a put-back that can't land exactly no longer repeats every pass.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Review fixes: a change refused because a claim or handover hadn't synced yet waits (up to 10 min) instead of being dropped, and authority is judged by who drove at the time; malformed events/manifests or conflict copies can't stall or repeat; Live sync survives any error in a tick; insert/remove bars applies the map it carries and its edits wait for it (late joiners replay correctly); a take deleted without the right comes back; claims are never wiped by a failed read and keep their own dates, Release mine asks; Solo checkout always takes the newer project and reuses identical prints; safer file replace on Windows; import does one take index per pass.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Taking control no longer shows a dialog (it paused Live sync); time claims show the bars they cover and keep their own date; a bad manifest names what's missing; Syncthing starts from a path with an apostrophe; the Mac installer reports a failed install; README lists the remaining limits.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Claim and take-back labels count bars from the tempo map (the displayed position rounded 4.999 s into the next bar: '2.5-5.0 s' read 'bars 2-3').

version.author: James
version.changelog: Concurrent edits converge: when two people change one take or fader at once, the newest change wins on every machine (a fast clock can't freeze a take). Same-second claims and handovers are decided the same way everywhere. Solo lock conflict copies are tidied on release.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Undoing one of BandSync's own changes no longer gets redone at once (Live sync waits 30 s so you can keep undoing, e.g. back to your own track delete). Your own events count as seen (a clock that ran ahead can't outrank your later changes). Moving a bandmate's take moves its MIDI copy too. Live sync says so when its tab is closed. Solo edit won't open a second tab of a solo copy that's still open.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A take that comes back after a delete you weren't allowed to make is put back as it was here (position, trim, lane, mute), not as it was first sent.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Undoing a delete you sent brings the take back for the band too (its files come out of the trash and an undelete goes out); if it's no longer yours to change, it's removed again with a message.

version.author: James
version.changelog: New: Send selection. Sends what's highlighted: selected items, every item on selected tracks, or everything in a time selection; with a time selection, only its inside (items crossing its edges are split there) or whole items; optionally every take of each item. Works from any project too: pick the song and the takes land there at the same bar and beat (warns when the tempo differs). Replaces Send takes in the panel.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Send selection: the menu (with 'every take of each item') also shows when there's no time selection.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Send selection: nothing is split until you confirm; the dialog says which stretch goes and that outside parts stay; tempo warning only for the stretch sent (and names both tempos); song/room pickers have headers; counts read '1 item (2 takes)'; menus don't jump; no undo point unless something was split.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side is saved with the song (a closed and reopened tab used to come back with it off, so it ignored the band's play/stop). SonoBus rejoins under your BandSync name even if the server renamed you once (e.g. 'Laptop 4').

version.author: James
version.changelog: Installers (from the first real Mac run): the password prompt is explained before it appears; REAPER is asked to close properly (save prompt included) and the installer waits for it, then reopens the project you had open; no 'send the host your ID' when you're already connected; Syncthing's default folder location is only set on a fresh setup.

version.author: James
version.changelog: New song chooser: Open session, Solo edit and Send selection (from another project) open one searchable window instead of a long menu: most recent activity first, with host, who's in it and when, the room picked right there (or a new side room typed in), Enter/Esc, and right-click to hide old or test songs on this machine. Installers sign Tailscale in as a tagged band machine, so it never has to sign in again (the host adds one tagOwners line to the tailnet policy once); a machine whose key expiry was turned off by hand is left alone.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The host lets new band machines into the shared folder by itself when they ask over the band's Tailscale (anything else waits for 'Let in' in the panel's Bandmates). Messages go to a new Activity list in the panel instead of popping the console up. Send selection asks at most one plain question (the part inside the time selection, the whole clips, or everything in those bars), asks about other takes only when a clip has them, and warns when Live sync is off. macOS: background checks and launching Syncthing/NINJAM work again (quoted commands never ran), and the Syncthing check no longer freezes the UI. Installers turn on 'Start Live sync with REAPER' and restart REAPER so your tabs come back.

version.author: James
version.changelog: New: Prepare this project for BandSync (panel: More, and the first screen). A checklist for an already busy project, done after a backup copy as one undo: multi-take items into fixed lanes keeping the playing take, 24-bit FLAC recording at one sample rate, unnamed/duplicate track names, WAV/AIFF converted to FLAC (verified sample by sample, originals kept in 'BandSync originals', 32-bit float left alone), outside files copied in, empty items and slivers removed, ripple editing off, SonoBus on the master, Live sync with REAPER. Chooser and checklist windows are opaque; the autostart toggle no longer reports a false failure.
